text: <blocked>bad() declares `int *data;` and immediately passes it, still uninitialized, to printIntPtrLine(data), which unconditionally executes `printf("%d\n", *intNumber)` - there is no NULL check or any other guard before the dereference. Every call to bad() therefore dereferences a wild, indeterminate stack pointer, which is undefined behavior (very likely an invalid memory read, and even when it happens to land on mapped memory the printed value is whatever garbage byte pattern happens to be on the stack, so the output is not deterministic and depends on the compiler, optimization level and prior stack contents rather than on any input). This is exactly what AddressSanitizer/UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer are meant to catch, and it is baked into bad() itself: the function takes no parameters, so a caller has no way to supply a valid pointer or otherwise make the call safe. Because bad is a mandatory listed symbol that must be called directly and is also reached through driver(0), and no input exists that avoids the dereference, no driver satisfying the "never trigger undefined behavior / sanitizer-clean / deterministic output" requirements can be written for this unit.</blocked>
